name: keplertitan
description: NVIDIA GeForce GTX TITAN (GK110, Kepler, sm_35) at its 837 MHz base clock: one Vortex core per SMX.

sources.NUM_CORES, NUM_WARPS, NUM_THREADS, ISSUE: 14 SMX (2688 CUDA cores), 64 resident warps per SMX, 4 warp schedulers each with 2 dispatch units (NVIDIA Kepler GK110 whitepaper)
sources.NUM_ALU_LANES, NUM_FPU_LANES, NUM_LSU_LA: GK110 SMX: 192 FP32/INT32 cores, 64 FP64 units, 32 LD/ST units and 32 SFUs over 4 schedulers (GK110 whitepaper). Vortex lanes divide the warp, so each scheduler's block gets 32 lanes (128 per SMX): the other 64 cores are reached on the part only by dual-issuing independent instructions, which Vortex does not model. fp32_lanes (2688) is therefore not checked
sources.FMA64_PE_RATIO: 64 FP64 units per SMX, 16 per scheduler (GK110 whitepaper; the TITAN runs FP64 at the full 1/3 rate with its double-precision mode on): 32 FPU lanes / 2 = 16 F64 FMA PEs per block, the part's FP64 lanes
sources.FDIV_PE_RATIO, FSQRT_PE_RATIO, FCVT_PE_R: 32 results per clock per SMX, 8 per scheduler: FP32 reciprocal and reciprocal square root, on which division and square root are built, and the 32-bit type conversions (CUDA C++ Programming Guide, arithmetic instruction throughput, compute capability 3.5); 32 FPU lanes / 4
sources.NUM_MUFU_LANES: 32 SFUs per SMX, 8 per scheduler (GK110 whitepaper)
sources.DCACHE_SIZE, DCACHE_NUM_WAYS: 16 KB L1 with 48 KB shared memory, the default split of the 64 KB L1/shared per SMX (GK110 whitepaper): 4 ways
sources.LMEM_SIZE, LMEM_LOG_SIZE, LMEM_NUM_BANKS: 48 KB shared memory per SMX; 32 banks of 8 B (GK110 shared memory runs in an 8-byte bank mode, 256 B per clock)
sources.L2_SIZE, L2_NUM_WAYS, L2_NUM_BANKS: 1.5 MB L2 (GK110 whitepaper): 24 ways over power-of-two sets; 16 banks with the 16 modelled channels
sources.PLATFORM_MEMORY_TYPE, PLATFORM_MEMORY_NU: 384-bit GDDR5 at 6 Gbps (288.4 GB/s) modelled as 16 GDDR6 x16 channels at 9013 MT/s for a power-of-two interleave: 16 x 2 B x 9.013 GT/s = 288.4 GB/s, the card's bandwidth
sources.PLATFORM_CLOCK_RATE: 837 MHz base clock (876 MHz boost), the clock of Accel-Sim's SM3_KEPLER_TITAN configuration
sources.EXT_TCU_ENABLE: Kepler has no tensor cores and no RT cores
sources.VM_ENABLE, EXT_A_ENABLE, EXT_ZACAS_ENABL: Kepler has a unified virtual address space behind an MMU, global and shared-memory atomics with atomicCAS, FP16 conversion, special-function units, 16 named barriers (bar.sync 0-15) and the graphics pipeline of a GeForce part
sources.CP_LLC_CLIENT: Host copies reach device memory through the L2 like every other client, so uploaded data is L2-resident at launch
sources.reference: dram_bandwidth_gbs is the vendor peak. Checked by ci/profile_check.py. Latencies: L1 hit 35 cycles on the K80's GK210 (Jia et al., Dissecting the NVIDIA Turing T4 GPU via Microbenchmarking (arXiv 1903.07486), Table 3.1), L2 hit 198 and global memory 339 cycles on the GTX 780, a GK110 like this card (Mei and Chu, Dissecting GPU Memory Hierarchy through Microbenchmarking (IEEE TPDS 2017, arXiv 1509.02308), Figure 14). Accel-Sim correlates this card: GPGPU-Sim tested-cfg SM3_KEPLER_TITAN and posted hardware runs (kepler-titan)
sources.L1_LINK_LATENCY: 4 core cycles each way between a core and its dcache, the L1/texture load pipeline, which the dcache bank pipeline (DCACHE_LATENCY) does not model: calibrated with ci/profile_check.py so the SimX pointer chase gives the 35-cycle L1 hit latency in 'reference'
sources.L2_LINK_LATENCY: 66 core cycles each way between an SM and the L2, the SM-to-L2 network: calibrated with ci/profile_check.py (after the L1 link) so the SimX pointer chase gives the 198-cycle L2 hit latency in 'reference'
sources.PLATFORM_MEMORY_LATENCY: 83 core cycles of PHY/NoC latency beyond the links, calibrated with ci/profile_check.py so the SimX cold pointer chase gives the 339-cycle global memory latency in 'reference'
sources.L2_MSHR_SIZE: 64 per bank: Little's law on the L2-miss round trip (DRAM 339 - L2 hit 198 = 141 cycles) x 345 B/cycle (288.4 GB/s / 837 MHz) / (16 banks x 64 B) = 47.5, rounded up to a power of two. The derived default counts only PLATFORM_MEMORY_LATENCY, which the links mostly replace
